name: 3.5 mm headphone socket
summary: Panel-mount audio jack for ordinary headphones. Needs a 6 mm round hole.
source: The 3.5 mm plug itself is standard: a 3.5 mm barrel about 14 mm long. The socket around it is not standardised. The cheap threaded panel jacks (PJ-392 and lookalikes) use a 6 mm threaded barrel and so need a 6 mm hole, but studio-grade jacks such as the Neutrik NYS229 use a 9.5 mm barrel and need a 9.5 mm hole. Nothing behind the panel is verified: body length, body shape and lug positions differ between suppliers. Measure the barrel on the jack you actually bought before drilling.

keepouts.label: Room for the plug and cable

electrical.note: Carries a line-level or headphone-level audio signal, well under a volt in normal use. This is not a power connector.
